entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.5198 Of 2019
Order:

1. The petitioner/accused seeks to quash the proceedings against him in C.C. No.469 of 2019, on the file of learned I Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate, Tenali, Guntur district (for short, 'the trial Court'), which was taken cognizance for the offences under Sections 420, 272, 273 and 188 of IPC and Sections 57, 58, 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the FSS Act').
2.

entities.text: I Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate, Tenali, Guntur district
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that, on 18.04.2019 at 05.30 P.M., on receiving the credible information, the complainant along with his staff proceeded to railway bridge, near Vykuntapuram temple, Tenali, and found the petitioner/accused, who is running a buddy shop, in possession of banned tobacco products, purchased from some unknown person for selling the same to consumers on higher price, and on interrogation as the accused voluntarily confessed to have been engaged in the business of prohibited tobacco products, seized the contraband, registered F.I.R. for the offences stated supra and released the accused on his self bail.

3. Learned counsel for petitioner while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore the police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He UDPR,J relied upon the common order of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the Criminal Petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto on the report of Sub-Inspector of Police, Tenali I Town Police Station.
Therefore, it is violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned, and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

5. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this Criminal Petition is allowed quashing the proceedings against the petitioner/accused in C.C. No.469 of 2019, on the file learned I G.Venkata Koteswara Rao vs State Of Ap on 16 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198603347/
1 Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate, Tenali, which was taken cognizance for the aforesaid offences.
